_owner: Track D writes criteria; Track A implements checks. v1 = the 6 repo checks + 6 process criteria with "v1": true; the rest is the full catalog (SHOULD).
_fields: check = how layer 1 decides from the GitHub API. judge = the question the LLM-judge answers from retrieve() results, with a quote as evidence. first_step = shown when status is missing/partial. expected_brightline = what the audit should find on the demo corpus (use it as a test).

repo_checks.title: README has Getting started
repo_checks.check: README.md exists and has a heading matching /getting started|quick ?start|setup/i
repo_checks.first_step: Add a 'Getting started' section to the README with the first 3–5 steps and links to the setup guide.

repo_checks.title: Setup guide + known issues
repo_checks.check: a file matching /setup|install|getting-started/i in docs/ AND a file matching /known.?issues|troubleshoot|faq/i
repo_checks.first_step: Write docs/setup.md as numbered steps with a check after each step, and docs/known-issues.md with exact error texts.

repo_checks.title: CONTRIBUTING with review conventions
repo_checks.check: CONTRIBUTING.md exists and mentions review prefixes (/nit:|blocking:|must|optional/i)
repo_checks.first_step: Add a 'Review conventions' table to CONTRIBUTING.md (what is required vs optional).

repo_checks.title: PR template has How to test
repo_checks.check: .github/pull_request_template.md exists and has a heading matching /how to test|testing|test plan/i
repo_checks.first_step: Add a 'How to test' section to the PR template.
repo_checks.expected_brightline: partial (template exists, only Summary + Related issue)

repo_checks.title: Issue templates with acceptance criteria
repo_checks.check: files in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ and at least one mentions /acceptance criteria/i
repo_checks.first_step: Add a feature template with an 'Acceptance criteria' checklist.

repo_checks.title: Recent issues have acceptance criteria
repo_checks.check: % of the last 30 issues whose body matches /acceptance criteria|- \[ \]/i; pass ≥ 70%, partial ≥ 30%
repo_checks.first_step: Add acceptance criteria to open issues before they are assigned to a junior.

repo_checks.title: At least 3 good first issues
repo_checks.check: open issues with label 'good first issue' ≥ 3
repo_checks.first_step: Label 3 small, well-described issues as 'good first issue'.

repo_checks.title: CODEOWNERS
repo_checks.first_step: Add a CODEOWNERS file so juniors know who reviews what.

repo_checks.title: Markdown images have alt text
repo_checks.check: count Markdown images with empty alt (/!\[\s*\]\(/) in all .md files; 0 = pass
repo_checks.first_step: Add alt text that says what each image shows.

repo_checks.title: ARCHITECTURE and ADRs
repo_checks.check: ARCHITECTURE.md (or docs/architecture*) AND at least one file in docs/adr/
repo_checks.first_step: Write a one-page ARCHITECTURE.md and start recording decisions as ADRs.
repo_checks.expected_brightline: pass (only ADR-007 in the repo; 001–006 are 'in the old wiki')

repo_checks.title: README and setup guide are easy to read
repo_checks.check: Flesch reading ease of README.md and the setup guide ≥ 50, average sentence length ≤ 20 words
repo_checks.first_step: Shorten long sentences and use numbered steps.

process_criteria.title: Written Definition of Done
process_criteria.judge: Is there a written Definition of Done that lists concrete conditions?
process_criteria.first_step: Write a Definition of Done with 5–7 checkable conditions.

process_criteria.title: Buddy for juniors
process_criteria.judge: Does every new or junior engineer get an assigned buddy or mentor who is not their manager?
process_criteria.first_step: Assign a buddy (not the manager) to every new engineer for at least 3 months.

process_criteria.title: Async standup allowed
process_criteria.judge: Can people give their standup update in writing instead of speaking?
process_criteria.first_step: Allow written standup updates in a thread before the call.

process_criteria.title: Captions/transcripts for ceremonies
process_criteria.judge: Do team ceremonies and trainings have captions or a written transcript?
process_criteria.first_step: Turn on captions for planning, refinement and retro, and share notes afterwards.
process_criteria.expected_brightline: partial (Handbook 4.3: only Pulse is captioned; ceremonies are not recorded)

process_criteria.title: Agenda in advance + written follow-up
process_criteria.judge: Are agendas shared before meetings and decisions written down afterwards?
process_criteria.first_step: Post the agenda the day before and decisions in the channel after.

process_criteria.title: Focus time and notification norms
process_criteria.judge: Are there written norms for focus time, meeting-free time or notifications?
process_criteria.first_step: Agree on meeting-free blocks and when people may be pinged.

process_criteria.title: Adjustments process incl. assistive tech
process_criteria.judge: Is there a written process to request workplace adjustments, with a response time, and does it cover assistive technology?
process_criteria.first_step: Add a response time (e.g. 10 working days) and assistive technology (screen readers, captioning) to the policy.
process_criteria.expected_brightline: partial (policy exists; no response time, no assistive tech, no appeal)

process_criteria.title: Accessible tooling (WCAG 2.2 / EN 301 549)
process_criteria.judge: Do internal tools have to meet an accessibility standard, and how are problems reported?
process_criteria.first_step: Require WCAG 2.2 AA for internal tools you buy or build.
process_criteria.expected_brightline: partial (Handbook 7: 'should work with keyboard and screen reader', no standard named)

process_criteria.title: Accessible pair programming
process_criteria.judge: Is pair programming done in a way that works for screen reader users or people who can't follow a shared screen?
process_criteria.first_step: Use Live Share or similar so each person pairs in their own editor.

process_criteria.title: Deferred on-call + accessible runbooks
process_criteria.judge: Do new engineers join on-call later, and does every alert have a written runbook?
process_criteria.first_step: Defer on-call for new joiners and link a runbook to every alert.

process_criteria.title: Health data confidentiality (GDPR art. 9)
process_criteria.judge: Does a company document state that health information employees share (for example for an adjustment request) is confidential, or say who is allowed to see it? Rules about customer data do not count.
process_criteria.first_step: Add a confidentiality clause: only the People team sees health details; the manager sees only the agreed adjustments.
process_criteria.expected_brightline: missing (the policy has no confidentiality clause and points to a public Slack channel)

process_criteria.title: RO obligations from 50 employees (4% quota, OUG 127/2024)
process_criteria.judge: Does the company mention its obligations under Law 448/2006 (4% employment quota from 50 employees, as amended by OUG 127/2024)?
process_criteria.first_step: Check the headcount and how the 4% quota is met, and write it down.
process_criteria.expected_brightline: missing (34 engineers, total headcount not in the docs: report as 'no evidence found')
